claims.statement: libs/evals is an end-to-end behavioral evaluation suite for the Deep Agents SDK: each eval runs an agent against a real LLM, captures the full trajectory (tool calls, file mutations, final response), and scores it on correctness and efficiency.

Evals score the agent trajectory with a two-tier assertion model: TrajectoryScorer.success(...) assertions are correctness checks that hard-fail the test, while .expect(...) assertions are trajectory-shape efficiency expectations that are logged but never fail the test.
Each eval is a @pytest.mark.langsmith test function that accepts a model fixture, builds the agent with create_deep_agent(...), and drives it via run_agent(...) passing a TrajectoryScorer.
EVAL_CATALOG.md is auto-generated from tests/evals/ by scripts/generate_eval_catalog.py and lists every eval grouped by category; it must not be edited by hand.
deepagents-evals run shells out to `uv run --group test pytest tests/evals` from libs/evals, forwarding --model and every category/tier/provider flag through to tests/evals/conftest.py.

The --model value may be omitted when the DEEPAGENTS_EVALS_MODEL environment variable is set; the explicit flag wins when both are set, and if neither resolves the CLI exits with a configuration error listing known model groups.

Because the pytest_reporter plugin rewrites pytest's session exit status to 0 even when individual evals fail, the CLI determines trial/aggregate failure from the aggregated counts.failed.mean in trials_summary.json rather than from the per-trial pytest_returncode.

deepagents-evals model-groups --check and catalog --check are drift detectors whose non-zero exit is mapped to the configuration exit code (2) meaning the generated file is stale, distinct from an eval-failure exit.

The eval suite refuses to start unless LANGSMITH_TRACING=true and LANGSMITH_API_KEY are set, because conftest.py aborts the run when they are missing and every eval logs inputs, outputs, and feedback via langsmith.testing.

A trials run writes per-trial evals_report_trial_NNN.json files (metrics plus a failures array) and an aggregated trials_summary.json carrying mean/median/stdev/min/max for correctness, solve rate, step/tool-call ratios, duration, pass-fail counts, and per-category scores.

deepagents_harbor/langgraph_project/langgraph.json is the source of truth for the packages the Harbor agent environment installs, and Makefile targets (run-hello-world, run-terminal-bench-*) drive Harbor across backends after make stage-harbor-local-deps stages checked-out packages for the sandbox install.
Unified evals score each axis on pass@K (fraction of tasks passing in at least one of K rollouts) except graded axes such as research, which report avg@K because their pass@K is 0 by construction.
The normal libs/evals test target runs pytest against tests/unit_tests with non-Unix sockets disabled, while make evals separately invokes the real-model tests/evals suite.

Within one run_trials invocation, trials run sequentially because concurrent in-process LangSmith experiment creation and provider rate limits are unsafe; CI instead parallelizes separate jobs and merges reports with aggregate-only.
The Harbor LangGraph agent removes provider and LangSmith credential variables while performing shell operations and restores them afterward, preventing task commands from inheriting those secrets.

run_agent creates invocation inputs from the query, optional initial files, and extra state; invokes the compiled graph with a thread ID; logs inputs and outputs to LangSmith; converts the mapping result into an AgentTrajectory; and applies the optional scorer.

The eval pytest configuration filters collected tests by repeatable category and tier markers, gives category exclusions precedence over inclusions, and exits when a requested filter value does not match a collected marker.

Deterministic product regression tests are package-owned: the deepagents and code Makefiles run unit tests by default with network sockets disabled except Unix sockets, while their integration targets select a separate integration-test directory.

The reusable Harbor workflow validates required LangSmith, model-provider, verifier, and research web-search credentials before sandbox execution; it rejects unknown sandbox environments and missing secrets rather than running a materially incomplete benchmark.

The reusable Harbor workflow passes a caller-supplied flat matrix through to leaf jobs, runs it with fail-fast disabled, and derives one aggregation entry per category and agent implementation with the expected shard count.
For branch comparisons, the Harbor workflow validates and fetches the resolved branch SHA, overlays only the four agent-under-test libraries, and leaves the Harbor harness at the workflow revision.
The DeepAgentsLangGraph Harbor adapter forwards the task's skills_dir into configurable state, because that is Harbor's LangGraph runner channel into the graph factory.
The Harbor-agent unit tests assert the registered dcode, bare, and tau3 graph keys, test web-search key gating and bounds, and verify credential scrubbing while graph construction occurs.

The unified prep policy maps autonomous to harbor-index with a selectable code graph, conversation to a pinned tau3 graph, context to a local context-retrieval dataset, and research to a local DRBench dataset; only fan-out categories multiply across selected code graphs.

Unified prep validates task profile and exact task selections before building work, uses frozen lite tasks or enumerated full-profile tasks, and fails instead of running an empty or unknown selection.

Unified prep derives per-model and global runner pools from a 40-task-per-model and 80-runner budget, rejects over-cap outer matrices and branch counts, and rejects a post-pack unified run above the 400-job budget.

Research is a category-specific unified override: it pins an arm64 runner, Docker sandbox, and concurrency 1 because DRBench images are arm64-only and its application stack is too disk-heavy for concurrent rollout jobs.

The reusable Harbor workflow gives Tavily only to research, validates DRBench judge compatibility, and visibly falls back to gpt-5.6-luna for an unsupported research judge without changing the suite-wide judge used elsewhere.

A shared experiment_name helper deterministically derives each Harbor LangSmith project name from leaf identity, raw-branch hash, workflow run and attempt, and optional reasoning effort; prep, Harbor execution, and aggregation all call it to prevent logging and usage-query drift.

Unified aggregation validates leaf summary schema and rollout count, preserves an expected leaf grid so missing artifacts mark rows incomplete, quarantines duplicate leaves, ranks rows by macro avg@K, and emits radar data only when at least three categories are present.

The unified workflow isolates best-effort LangSmith usage collection from repository publishing: the usage job receives the LangSmith key and only contents-read permission, while the combine job has contents-write permission and downloads usage artifacts without the key.
